failing.note: The observation is true and the claim holds. The snapshot is a git clone, so its entries keep git's modes (0755 and 0644 under umask 022), but it sits inside a lab home at 0700 beneath a store at 0700, and everything the verbs themselves write there was seen at 0700 or 0600. No other account can reach it, so the store is private to the account as the sentence says. The parenthetical describes the store's own levels and files, not the modes inside the cloned world; reading it as a promise about every entry of a clone is over-literal and nothing is exposed or misleading.

_reviewProvenance: Full tier for an additive release: both directions, the manifest's 50 checkers (Direction A over the 45 brief docs, Direction B over the 5 surfaces), each reading its prompt verbatim from a file holding the manifest's pinned context and direction template filled for its item, run by hand through the host's agent tool as Opus 5.5 agents against an exact export with the binary built from it. Two groups first ran a neighbouring group's items, so 14 items ran later; the coverage of all 50 was checked against the plan, and 14 items were read twice. Findings merged by the detector's merge (where plus the first sixty characters of claim, first kept): 133. Each was then re-verified against the tree and binary by a separate triage agent before its disposition. Checkers shared a scratch directory for a time, so triage did not rely on their scratch results.
